subject.title: [RFC] Multi-Session Architecture: Shared LLM + Isolated Sessions + Public Knowledge Base

question: Should this broad RFC remain the core umbrella for multi-session architecture, and which slices should be accepted into OpenClaw core versus narrowed into existing session-family, WebChat, or memory-plugin trackers?
rationale: The remaining work crosses product architecture and security boundaries; automation cannot safely choose a data model, memory-sharing policy, or core/plugin ownership boundary from source inspection alone.

options.title: Keep And Split The Umbrella
options.body: Keep this issue open for maintainer scoping, then create or link narrow staged issues for routing/mainKey, session-family memory boundaries, WebChat lifecycle, and memory/RAG policy.

options.title: Supersede With Narrow Trackers
options.body: Close this later only after maintainers explicitly move each remaining accepted slice to canonical issues such as the topic-session family and WebChat trackers.

options.title: Reject The Broad Architecture
options.body: Close the RFC as too broad for core and keep only concrete user-facing bugs or plugin/API extension requests that fit the current roadmap.

recommendation.title: Keep And Split The Umbrella
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for maintainer scoping, then create or link narrow staged issues for routing/mainKey, session-family memory boundaries, WebChat lifecycle, and memory/RAG policy.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the clearest product-routing owner from the issue mentions, related canonical-tracker comments, and recent session/routing/UI history.
